title: vNext View Vocabulary
description: Vocabulary for vNext platform-owned view and schema extensions. Provides reusable definitions for x-* fields consumed by backend, JSON Schema validators, and UI renderers.

x-errorMessages.description: Localized messages keyed by JSON Schema validation keyword. The runtime looks a failed keyword up by its name (JsonSchemaValidationMapper: ResolveErrorMessage(error.Key)), so any keyword it validates can carry one; the list below is the set the definitions use.

x-enum.description: Localized display labels keyed by enum value.

x-order.description: A field's position when a client generates a form from the schema; lower first, a field without one after every ordered field. Needed because a stored schema does not keep its property order (PostgreSQL jsonb normalises object keys).

roleGrantCondition.description: One role in an allOf/anyOf list: only a role name, a predefined instance role or a dynamic expression. No grant and no nesting (depth 1).

role.description: Role name (e.g. morph-idm.initiator) or dynamic expression (e.g. $userBehalfOf.$.context.Instance.Data.initial.customer.ownerUserId).

roleGrant.description: A single role grant: a role name, predefined instance role ($InstanceStarter, …) or dynamic expression ($user./$userBehalfOf./$role. + $.context.<path>), with allow or deny. Exactly one of role, allOf (all listed roles required) or anyOf (at least one listed role) selects who the grant applies to.

role.description: Role name (e.g. morph-idm.initiator) or dynamic expression (e.g. $userBehalfOf.$.context.Instance.Data.initial.customer.ownerUserId).

allOf.description: Conjunction: the caller must hold every listed role.

anyOf.description: Disjunction: the caller must hold at least one listed role.

x-roles.description: Role-based visibility/permission grants for a view or field. Roles may be domain-qualified names or dynamic expressions. DENY overrides ALLOW.

x-filterOperators.description: Allowed filter operators for this field, spelled as the runtime matches a DECLARATION: a list query's operator token is mapped to these names before the check (ne → neq, ge → gte, le → lte, like/match → contains, startswith → startsWith, endswith → endsWith, isnull → isNull), so declaring the query token itself (e.g. 'ge') makes every such filter fail with 'Operator is not allowed'. Empty or absent means the field is not filterable. Semantics depend on the field's JSON type (number/integer: numeric compare; string + gt/gte/lt/lte/between: date compare; string + eq/contains/startsWith/endsWith: text compare; boolean: equality; array: includes).

x-sortable.description: When true, the field is sortable. Absent means not sortable.

filterExpression.description: Dynamic request filter parameter resolved from form, instance, or component parameters.

param.description: Request parameter name. May carry the list-query operator after a colon ('status:in'); without one the backend's default (equality) applies.

value.description: A literal, or a reference resolved by the client ('$form.<path>', '$instance.<path>', '$param.<name>'). A LITERAL may be an array, which is the only way to reach the 'in' / 'nin' operators; a reference is always a string.

x-lov.description: List-of-values definition for dropdown and selection components. The options come from a data SOURCE (a URN, fetched) or from ITEMS already in scope (an expression, no request) — exactly one of the two.

source.description: URN of the data source function. May interpolate '{{$form.x}}' / '{{$instance.x}}' / '{{$param.x}}' to choose WHICH source (e.g. a domain picked in a sibling field); an unresolved placeholder skips the load.

items.description: An expression ('$instance.<path>' / '$form.<path>') naming an array already in scope; the options are built from it with no request. valueField/displayField are then plain property names within one element, or empty to use the element itself (a list of strings).

valueField.description: Path to the option value: a JSONPath into the fetched envelope with 'source', a plain property name (or empty = the element) with 'items'.

displayField.description: Path to the option label — same two shapes as valueField.

imageField.description: Path to an image for each option, for pickers that draw one (same path shape as valueField).

source.description: URN of the data source function.

resultField.description: JSONPath expression for the returned object.

x-conditional.description: Conditional visibility and enablement rules for a schema property.

x-encryption.description: Field encryption; 'source' selects WHO encrypts. source 'runtime' (the default when absent) — AT REST: Encryption and data-classification metadata for a field. 'hash' is applied when the data is written: the stored (and served) value is HASHED:SHA256:<hex> (or SHA512), an HMAC under a salt the runtime generates for each instance — irreversible, so it takes no roles. 'encrypt' stores the value as an AES-256-GCM token (ENCRYPTED:AES256:i1:<base64url>) in the instance data and decrypts it on load, so the engine works on plaintext; on the read surfaces a caller in the exemption list sees the plaintext and every other caller the stored token. The key is generated by the runtime for each instance and kept in the flow schema's InstanceSecrets table, never in the schema. Only instance data is encrypted: transition bodies, task journals, events and caches are not (yet). 'none' declares no encryption. 'persisted' and 'transport' were removed (never enforced; use 'encrypt'). An active type (other than 'none') cannot be combined with x-masking, x-filterOperators, x-sortable or x-indexed on the same property, and only applies to string properties reachable through nested 'properties'. source 'client' — IN TRANSIT, client → backend: the client seals the value to the recipient's public key before the request leaves, and only the service holding the private key opens it; 'key' and 'algorithm' are required and the at-rest members are not accepted. The runtime does nothing with a 'client' rule (no at-rest encryption, no read masking, no filter refusal). A client that cannot seal REFUSES the write — it never sends the plaintext. By role: a master (record) schema accepts both — 'runtime' is applied at rest, 'client' is accepted and left untouched by the runtime; a transition / function-input (input) schema accepts source 'client' only.

source.description: WHO encrypts. 'runtime' (default when absent): at rest — the runtime encrypts or hashes the stored value (type, params, roles, redactInLogs, retentionDays). 'client': in transit, client → backend — the client seals the value before the request leaves (key, algorithm, into, encoding, nonce, envelope); the runtime accepts it on any schema and does nothing with it.

params.description: Parameters of type 'hash'. No salt or key may appear here.

roles.description: Allow-only EXEMPTION list: a caller matching an allow grant sees the raw value; every other caller (unlisted, misspelled or missing roles) sees it transformed. deny is not accepted. Not accepted for type 'hash' (hashed on write, irreversible).

purpose.description: Data classification of the field (e.g. PII, PII-Identification, Financial, Credential). Metadata for tooling and governance; not enforced by the runtime.

redactInLogs.description: Declares that the value must never appear in logs. The runtime's own structured logs never carry instance data; this flag is for tooling and log pipelines and is not enforced by the runtime.

retentionDays.description: Retention period of the field in days. Metadata for governance; not enforced by the runtime.

key.description: source 'client': the recipient's public key — a context read address ('urn:client:context:read:<boundary>:<storage>:<key>') or '$instance.<path>'.

algorithm.description: source 'client': the sealing suite. HPKE (RFC 9180) DHKEM P-256 / HKDF-SHA256 / AES-128-GCM, or RSA-OAEP-256.

into.description: source 'client': the field the ciphertext is sent as; absent = in place.

nonce.description: source 'client': a per-record value bound into the sealed text ('{value}:{nonce}') as a replay guard.

x-encryption-client.description: x-encryption narrowed to source 'client' (in transit, client → backend) — the form a transition / function-input schema accepts.

x-masking.description: Master-schema field masking applied by the runtime on the caller-facing read surfaces (data function, instance GET/list, sync start/transition responses), after x-roles pruning. Stored data never changes. Only on type: string properties reachable through nested properties; cannot be combined with x-filterOperators, x-sortable or an active x-encryption.

operator.description: mask keeps keepFirst/keepLast characters and masks the middle (length-preserving); replace writes params.value.

roles.description: Allow-only EXEMPTION list: a caller matching an allow grant sees the raw value; every other caller (unlisted, misspelled or missing roles) sees it masked. deny is not accepted.

x-storage.description: Master-schema file offload: a property marked x-storage keeps its file bytes in the named Dapr binding component instead of in the instance data. binding is the name of the Dapr binding component.

binding.description: Name of the Dapr binding component that stores the file bytes.

x-validation.description: Backend-defined custom validation rule metadata. The rule 'remote' runs a backend function (source) on the field value and reads the outcome from its response (resultField, messageField).

source.description: Remote rule only: URN of the function the client calls to validate the value.

resultField.description: Remote rule only: path in the response whose truthy value means the value is valid.

messageField.description: Remote rule only: path in the response holding the message shown when the value is invalid.

trigger.description: Remote rule only: when the client calls the function.

debounce.description: Remote rule only: milliseconds to wait after the last change before calling the function.

viewDocument.description: Lightweight vNext view document root contract.
